components.role: Unchanged original-resolution 1900x1518 public photo of the actual Deal Me In box-lid scoring and condensed rules. All text and diagrams visually read. It explicitly says FULL RULES ENCLOSED; the separate full booklet remains unrecovered.

deal-me-in.evidence: Detailed English community rules account for the named 1988 Noraut Deal Me In poker-tile board game, BGG 2062, recovered in actual 4 June 2024 public archived HTML. The older requested archive timestamp redirected to this actual capture; it is not called a 2010 source. The published description was decoded statically from GEEK.geekitemPreload.item.description JSON and parsed as HTML text, with no JavaScript execution. It matches the independently cached current public account exactly. New public image-detail metadata offered the original 1900x1518 photograph of the matching box-lid reference, larger than the earlier 1024x818 image; that actual offered URL was retrieved, without inventing a CDN variant or bypassing access controls. All original-lid text and diagrams were individually read. The photo supplies nine exact poker-hand scores, legal/illegal placement illustrations, mandatory initial joker positions, highest-card starter, pair minimum and compulsory opening, ordinary/opening multiplier distinction, joker capture/naming, explicit finish conditions, final least-card payment and highest-point winner. The separate full community account supplies 11x11 board, 56 card tiles/four jokers/30 end stoppers/four racks/chips, initial 150 chips and seven-card hand, joker starting placement, turn placement versus exchanging tiles at ten each, building/interlocking scoring hands, matching-symbol bonuses and blocking completed five-card ends. Combined sources are a usable CORE RULES REFERENCE, accurately labelled third-party rules-reference HTML with a primary original-lid component; not a recovered full publisher booklet or certified transcription. The lid explicitly says FULL RULES ENCLOSED. Full refill/draw-pool exhaustion handling, every joker/multiplier interaction, ties and all original booklet edge cases are not independently established. The community account’s shorthand ending when cards run out is retained verbatim and explicitly distinguished from the primary lid’s no-cards/no-further-scoring-hand ending and payment. Canonical text separately labels short visually checked paraphrased primary facts and the complete unchanged-wording community description. No missing play procedure was invented from its Scrabble analogy. Original archived HTML and full-resolution photograph retain separate hashes. Actual board/tile set remains necessary. One specific MAJOR initial-joker/legal-opening finding is recorded directly against the original lid and supporting account; no full summary audit, PASS or summary-body repair.
